مُخَرْفَجٌ Ample: (K:) applied to anything. (TA.) It is said in a trad., كَرِهَ السَّرَاوِيلَ المُخَرْفَجَةَ He disliked, or disapproved of, ample trousers: (A 'Obeyd:) or they say it means trousers reaching down to the upper part of the foot. (S.) And you say, عَيْشٌ مُخَرْفَجٌ A plentiful life. (S.) ―
-b2- Also The best of food, or of meat and drink; and so ↓ خَرْفَجٌ and ↓ خُرَافِجٌ . (Er-Riyáshee.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
